claude.sample_unit: chatbot responses (9 NIH FAQs prompted/unprompted and 11 simulated presurgical messages across 4 LLMs; 254 citations)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of chatbot responses versus grade 8 target
links.effect: Mean reading level grade 12.9 unprompted; grade 10.5 even when prompted to write at grade 8; NIH website 9.8.
links.quote: Chatbots were unable to communicate at a grade 8 reading level, even when prompted to do so, responding at grade 10.5 (SD, 1.6).

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient education responses relative to recommended grade 8
links.effect: Average Flesch-Kincaid grade 12.9 (SD 2.5), above the recommended grade 8; prompted 10.5.
links.quote: All chatbots queried answered the unprompted queries at a reading level of 12.9 (SD, 2.5), which is above the recommended reading level of grade 8.

links.outcome: Validity of citations provided by LLM chatbots
links.effect: Of 254 citations, 108 (42.5%) appropriate; 101 (39.8%) cited source not real; 28 (11.0%) real source lacking the cited information.
links.quote: The examined chatbots appropriately cited sources in only 108 of 254 citations (42.5%).

links.outcome: DISCERN quality of responses with versus without a prompt
links.effect: Quality improved from mean 3.5/5 (moderate) unprompted to 4.6/5 (high) prompted; significant difference at P<.05.
links.quote: Without prompting, the quality of information was moderate, with a mean 3.5 of 5.0 (SD, 0.6) across all LLMs.

links.outcome: Chatbot refusal to answer patient questions
links.effect: Google Bard refused 3 of 11 presurgical questions, saying it was not a health care professional; other chatbots answered all.
links.quote: However, Google Bard refused to answer questions 3, 8, and 10, citing that it was not a health care professional and not qualified to give medical advice.

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM responses to simulated presurgical patient messages
links.effect: Mean accuracy 5.5/6 (SD 0.8) and completeness 2.8/3 (SD 0.4); no chatbot below 5.4 accuracy.
links.quote: LLMs were accurate and complete, with average scores of 5.5 of 6.0 (SD, 0.8) and 2.8 of 3.0 (SD, 0.4), respectively ( Table 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering by users (instructing chatbot on quality/reading level) to improve response quality

links.effect: Chatbots appropriately cited sources in only 42.5% (108/254) of citations, hallucinating sources in 39.8% (101/254), citing real sources without the cited information in 11.0% (28/254), and linking to different sources in 6.3% (16/254).
links.quote: The examined chatbots appropriately cited sources in only 108 of 254 citations (42.5%).

links.outcome: reading level of generated patient education responses
links.effect: Chatbots had an average reading level of grade 12.9 (SD, 2.5) unprompted and grade 10.5 (SD, 1.6) prompted, failing to communicate at the recommended grade 8 reading level.
links.quote: Chatbots were unable to communicate at a grade 8 reading level, even when prompted to do so, responding at grade 10.5 (SD, 1.6).

links.outcome: reading level of generated patient materials
links.effect: Average Flesch-Kincaid reading level was grade 12.9 (SD, 2.5) across unprompted queries and remained elevated at grade 10.5 (SD, 1.6) when prompted to communicate at grade 8.
links.quote: The average Flesch-Kincaid reading level was high, with a mean grade level of 12.9 (SD, 2.5; Table 1 ).
